scorecard.note: Add a more compelling narrative arc that connects the statistics to a personal story or vivid example, rather than just listing data points.

storyboard.ears: A safer sleep position transformed infant survival without ending the danger.
The SIDS rate fell to 0.64 per thousand births by 2008. Back sleeping accompanied a drop of more than half.
storyboard.evidence: CDC / NICHD | US SIDS rate per 1,000 live births, before vs. after Back to Sleep | https://safetosleep.nichd.nih.gov/about/history | 2026-10-06

storyboard.ears: Before the campaign, 85.4% of SIDS cases involved stomach-down placement. Sleep position became the prevention target.
storyboard.evidence: CDC / NICHD (Safe to Sleep) | Share of SIDS cases where the baby was placed stomach-down vs. back-up, before vs. after the campaign | https://safetosleep.nichd.nih.gov/about/history | 2026-10-06

storyboard.ears: About 3,400 sleep-related infant deaths still occur yearly. The improvement did not erase the need for safer sleep.
storyboard.evidence: CDC | Sleep-related infant deaths still recorded in the US each year | https://www.cdc.gov/sids/data.html | 2026-10-06

storyboard.ears: Putting babies on their backs remains a simple step parents can use tonight.
